dek: One practical guide examines how to verify agent outcomes, tool permissions, and side effects independently. No eligible HN stories or stable watchlist releases were found for October 18.

stories.title: An agent evaluation guide separates successful outcomes from permitted actions
stories.summary: The guide proposes explicit task boundaries, independent state assertions, and separate scoring for outcomes, permissions, and robustness. Its refund-agent example illustrates why completion alone cannot establish safe behavior.
body: An October 18 iTechGuides guide proposes evaluating an agent against a versioned task contract before interpreting its success rate. The contract specifies the starting state, required outcome, available tools, permission limits, prohibited side effects, and acceptable escalation. Its worked refund example distinguishes a completed payment from the authorization and audit steps that should precede it. The article recommends inspecting the resulting payment state independently rather than trusting an agent’s completion message.

The practical instrumentation requirement is to preserve tool arguments, authorization decisions, returned values, retries, latency, and relevant state changes alongside agent, policy, fixture, and evaluator versions. Outcome checks and permission checks remain separate: a forbidden action can invalidate an otherwise successful run, while a safe escalation can respect policy without completing the customer’s request. The guide also recommends segmenting failures by severity and workflow so averages do not conceal costly exceptions.

This is instructional synthesis with an illustrative scenario, not a measured deployment study or a new standard. Its operational value depends on implementing reliable fixtures, independent assertions, and appropriately protected traces; recording a trace alone does not prove that the final outcome was correct.
stories.takeaway: Pair each consequential tool action with an authorization record and an independent state check; report task completion and policy compliance as separate results.

image_provenance.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram
Asset type: standalone newspaper editorial infographic, PNG
Primary request: explain separate outcome and permission checks for an AI support-refund agent, based on https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-prove-your-ai-agent-works-a-practical-evals-and-safety-guide/
Source-supported facts: the guide recommends a versioned task contract, independent checks of the resulting state, and separate scoring of authorization and tool actions. A correct final state can coexist with a forbidden action. A safe escalation may leave the task incomplete while respecting permissions.
Style: warm ivory newsprint, crisp charcoal ink, muted rust and teal accents, restrained flat diagram, generous whitespace, newspaper serif title and readable sans-serif labels. Landscape, roughly 3:2.
Composition: title above a three-stage flow: Define contract, Run agent, Check evidence. Below the last stage show two equal independent check boxes, Outcome and Permissions, with simple document and key icons. At bottom show two short conceptual examples, each on its own line.
Text verbatim: 'Did the agent work safely?' ; 'Conceptual evaluation pattern'; 'Define contract'; 'Run agent'; 'Check evidence'; 'Outcome'; 'Verify final state'; 'Permissions'; 'Inspect tool actions'; 'Task completed + forbidden action = safety failure'; 'Safe escalation + incomplete task = separate scores'.
Constraints: no numerical performance claims, no product screenshot or logos, no extra footer or watermark. Keep the two checks visibly independent; use large text readable at article width.

stories.score_reason: Concrete trace requirements and independently checked side effects are directly useful, but this is guidance rather than new measured evidence.

source_evidence.method: Original publisher Article JSON-LD datePublished, confirmed against visible October 18, 2026 byline; raw HTML retained in agent-guide.html. dateModified not used.

research.note: Scoped sweep, not an exhaustive web search. Supplied discovery artifact preserved as discovery.json; discovery script was not rerun because this invocation restricts writes to the run directory. Official HN API checked all three IDs. GitHub APIs independently checked all eight watchlist repositories (701 release records), with no stable October 18 release. All six historical issues and 45 stories read before selection; full history and hashes in history-review.json. News surfaces retrieved and readable text preserved; focused exact-date searches supplemented configured sources. Guide is the publisher's own instructional synthesis, not a new NIST announcement or experimental result. Its task-contract and independent side-effect checks differ substantively from October 17's LLM-judge calibration guide.
